rules.name: Untrusted input expanded into an executed script

shortDescription.text: A ${{ }} expression carrying attacker-controlled text is substituted into a shell or script before it runs.

fullDescription.text: GitHub substitutes ${{ }} expressions into run: scripts (and script inputs such as actions/github-script's script) as text, before the interpreter parses them. Text that an outsider controls — a pull request title, a branch name, a comment, a commit message — becomes code that runs with the job's token and secrets. The engine follows the value through env:, GITHUB_ENV, step outputs, job outputs and local composite actions, and only reports sources the workflow's triggers can actually populate.

help.text:
GitHub substitutes ${{ }} expressions into run: scripts (and script inputs such as actions/github-script's script) as text, before the interpreter parses them. Text that an outsider controls — a pull request title, a branch name, a comment, a commit message — becomes code that runs with the job's token and secrets. The engine follows the value through env:, GITHUB_ENV, step outputs, job outputs and local composite actions, and only reports sources the workflow's triggers can actually populate.

Remediation: Pass the value through an environment variable and reference it as a shell variable ("$TITLE"), or as process.env in github-script, so it is data rather than code.
help.markdown:
GitHub substitutes ${{ }} expressions into run: scripts (and script inputs such as actions/github-script's script) as text, before the interpreter parses them. Text that an outsider controls — a pull request title, a branch name, a comment, a commit message — becomes code that runs with the job's token and secrets. The engine follows the value through env:, GITHUB_ENV, step outputs, job outputs and local composite actions, and only reports sources the workflow's triggers can actually populate.

**Remediation**

Pass the value through an environment variable and reference it as a shell variable ("$TITLE"), or as process.env in github-script, so it is data rather than code.

**Context used**

- repo

rules.name: Untrusted input written to GITHUB_ENV or GITHUB_PATH

shortDescription.text: Attacker-controlled text is appended to the job's environment or PATH file.

fullDescription.text: Lines appended to $GITHUB_ENV become environment variables for every later step, and lines appended to $GITHUB_PATH prepend directories to PATH. A value containing a newline can define LD_PRELOAD, NODE_OPTIONS, BASH_ENV or a new PATH entry, giving code execution in later steps even when those steps are written safely.

help.text:
Lines appended to $GITHUB_ENV become environment variables for every later step, and lines appended to $GITHUB_PATH prepend directories to PATH. A value containing a newline can define LD_PRELOAD, NODE_OPTIONS, BASH_ENV or a new PATH entry, giving code execution in later steps even when those steps are written safely.

Remediation: Do not write untrusted values to GITHUB_ENV/GITHUB_PATH. If a later step needs the value, pass it through a step output and env:, or use a random heredoc delimiter and validate the value first.
help.markdown:
Lines appended to $GITHUB_ENV become environment variables for every later step, and lines appended to $GITHUB_PATH prepend directories to PATH. A value containing a newline can define LD_PRELOAD, NODE_OPTIONS, BASH_ENV or a new PATH entry, giving code execution in later steps even when those steps are written safely.

**Remediation**

Do not write untrusted values to GITHUB_ENV/GITHUB_PATH. If a later step needs the value, pass it through a step output and env:, or use a random heredoc delimiter and validate the value first.

rules.name: Privileged workflow runs code from an untrusted pull request

shortDescription.text: A pull_request_target, workflow_run or comment-triggered job checks out the pull request's code and then executes it.

fullDescription.text: pull_request_target, workflow_run and issue_comment run in the base repository's context: a write-capable GITHUB_TOKEN and every secret. Checking out the pull request head and then running a script, a build, or a local action executes code the pull request author wrote with those privileges. Build scripts, package manager hooks, test configuration and local actions all count as execution.

help.text:
pull_request_target, workflow_run and issue_comment run in the base repository's context: a write-capable GITHUB_TOKEN and every secret. Checking out the pull request head and then running a script, a build, or a local action executes code the pull request author wrote with those privileges. Build scripts, package manager hooks, test configuration and local actions all count as execution.

Remediation: Split the work: run untrusted code under pull_request (no secrets, read-only token) and hand results to a privileged workflow as data via an artifact. If the privileged job must see the code, never execute it — and gate the job on an environment with required reviewers.

pull_request_target, workflow_run and issue_comment run in the base repository's context: a write-capable GITHUB_TOKEN and every secret. Checking out the pull request head and then running a script, a build, or a local action executes code the pull request author wrote with those privileges. Build scripts, package manager hooks, test configuration and local actions all count as execution.

**Remediation**

Split the work: run untrusted code under pull_request (no secrets, read-only token) and hand results to a privileged workflow as data via an artifact. If the privileged job must see the code, never execute it — and gate the job on an environment with required reviewers.

**Context used**

- repo
- environments

rules.name: Checkout credentials persisted into an uploaded workspace

shortDescription.text: actions/checkout writes the token into .git/config and the workspace is then uploaded as an artifact.

fullDescription.text: By default actions/checkout stores the job's GITHUB_TOKEN in .git/config so later git commands authenticate. Uploading the checkout directory as an artifact publishes that token to anyone who can download the run's artifacts — on a public repository, everyone — while the job is still running.

help.text:
By default actions/checkout stores the job's GITHUB_TOKEN in .git/config so later git commands authenticate. Uploading the checkout directory as an artifact publishes that token to anyone who can download the run's artifacts — on a public repository, everyone — while the job is still running.

Remediation: Set persist-credentials: false on actions/checkout, and upload only the build output directory, never the repository root.
help.markdown:
By default actions/checkout stores the job's GITHUB_TOKEN in .git/config so later git commands authenticate. Uploading the checkout directory as an artifact publishes that token to anyone who can download the run's artifacts — on a public repository, everyone — while the job is still running.

**Remediation**

Set persist-credentials: false on actions/checkout, and upload only the build output directory, never the repository root.

rules.name: Privileged workflow consumes artifacts from an untrusted run

shortDescription.text: A workflow_run job downloads artifacts produced by a fork-triggered run and extracts them into the workspace.

fullDescription.text: Artifacts uploaded by a pull_request run are written by the pull request's code. A workflow_run job that downloads them into the working directory lets that code overwrite scripts, configuration or binaries the privileged job then uses.

help.text:
Artifacts uploaded by a pull_request run are written by the pull request's code. A workflow_run job that downloads them into the working directory lets that code overwrite scripts, configuration or binaries the privileged job then uses.

Remediation: Download into a dedicated directory outside the workspace (e.g. ${{ runner.temp }}/artifacts), treat contents as untrusted data, and validate them before use. Never execute anything from the artifact.
help.markdown:
Artifacts uploaded by a pull_request run are written by the pull request's code. A workflow_run job that downloads them into the working directory lets that code overwrite scripts, configuration or binaries the privileged job then uses.

**Remediation**

Download into a dedicated directory outside the workspace (e.g. ${{ runner.temp }}/artifacts), treat contents as untrusted data, and validate them before use. Never execute anything from the artifact.

rules.name: Release workflow restores a cache writable by untrusted runs

shortDescription.text: A workflow that publishes releases restores dependency caches that other workflows on the default branch can write.

fullDescription.text: Caches are shared across workflows in the same branch scope. A compromised or injectable workflow on the default branch can save a poisoned cache entry that a release workflow later restores and ships inside a published artifact.

help.text:
Caches are shared across workflows in the same branch scope. A compromised or injectable workflow on the default branch can save a poisoned cache entry that a release workflow later restores and ships inside a published artifact.

Remediation: Disable caching in workflows that publish releases or sign artifacts (remove cache: / actions/cache), or use a cache key namespace no other workflow writes.
help.markdown:
Caches are shared across workflows in the same branch scope. A compromised or injectable workflow on the default branch can save a poisoned cache entry that a release workflow later restores and ships inside a published artifact.

**Remediation**

Disable caching in workflows that publish releases or sign artifacts (remove cache: / actions/cache), or use a cache key namespace no other workflow writes.

rules.name: Workflow token permissions not declared

shortDescription.text: Neither the workflow nor the job declares permissions:, so the token gets the repository default.

fullDescription.text: Without a permissions: block the GITHUB_TOKEN gets the repository or organisation default, which for many repositories is read/write on every scope. Any compromised step — a vulnerable action, an injection — can then push code, publish packages or approve pull requests.

help.text:
Without a permissions: block the GITHUB_TOKEN gets the repository or organisation default, which for many repositories is read/write on every scope. Any compromised step — a vulnerable action, an injection — can then push code, publish packages or approve pull requests.

Remediation: Add `permissions: {}` (or `contents: read`) at the top of the workflow, and grant individual jobs only the scopes they need.
help.markdown:
Without a permissions: block the GITHUB_TOKEN gets the repository or organisation default, which for many repositories is read/write on every scope. Any compromised step — a vulnerable action, an injection — can then push code, publish packages or approve pull requests.

**Remediation**

Add `permissions: {}` (or `contents: read`) at the top of the workflow, and grant individual jobs only the scopes they need.

**Context used**

- repo

rules.name: Excessive token permissions

shortDescription.text: The token is granted write-all, or write scopes at workflow level that every job inherits.

fullDescription.text: write-all grants every scope including actions, packages, pages and id-token. Workflow-level write scopes apply to every job, including jobs that run untrusted code or third-party actions.

help.text:
write-all grants every scope including actions, packages, pages and id-token. Workflow-level write scopes apply to every job, including jobs that run untrusted code or third-party actions.

Remediation: Use `permissions: {}` at the workflow level and grant each job only the specific scopes it needs.
help.markdown:
write-all grants every scope including actions, packages, pages and id-token. Workflow-level write scopes apply to every job, including jobs that run untrusted code or third-party actions.

**Remediation**

Use `permissions: {}` at the workflow level and grant each job only the specific scopes it needs.

rules.name: OIDC token minted outside a protected environment

shortDescription.text: A job with id-token: write is not bound to an environment with reviewers or a branch policy.

fullDescription.text: id-token: write lets the job request an OIDC token that cloud providers exchange for credentials. Cloud trust policies commonly match on repository only; without an environment gate, any branch, and any code that can run in that job, can obtain cloud credentials.

help.text:
id-token: write lets the job request an OIDC token that cloud providers exchange for credentials. Cloud trust policies commonly match on repository only; without an environment gate, any branch, and any code that can run in that job, can obtain cloud credentials.

Remediation: Bind the job to an environment with required reviewers or a protected-branch policy, and scope the cloud trust policy's subject to that environment (repo:owner/name:environment:prod).
help.markdown:
id-token: write lets the job request an OIDC token that cloud providers exchange for credentials. Cloud trust policies commonly match on repository only; without an environment gate, any branch, and any code that can run in that job, can obtain cloud credentials.

**Remediation**

Bind the job to an environment with required reviewers or a protected-branch policy, and scope the cloud trust policy's subject to that environment (repo:owner/name:environment:prod).

**Context used**

- environments

rules.name: All secrets passed to a reusable workflow

shortDescription.text: secrets: inherit hands every repository, environment and organisation secret to the called workflow.

fullDescription.text: The called workflow receives every secret the caller can see, not just the ones it uses. A reusable workflow in another repository, or one pinned to a mutable ref, becomes a way to exfiltrate all of them.

help.text:
The called workflow receives every secret the caller can see, not just the ones it uses. A reusable workflow in another repository, or one pinned to a mutable ref, becomes a way to exfiltrate all of them.

Remediation: Pass only the secrets the called workflow declares under on.workflow_call.secrets, by name.
help.markdown:
The called workflow receives every secret the caller can see, not just the ones it uses. A reusable workflow in another repository, or one pinned to a mutable ref, becomes a way to exfiltrate all of them.

**Remediation**

Pass only the secrets the called workflow declares under on.workflow_call.secrets, by name.

**Context used**

- repo

rules.name: Secrets context exposed in bulk

shortDescription.text: toJSON(secrets) or a computed secrets[...] index loads every secret into the job.

fullDescription.text: Secrets are only sent to a runner when referenced. toJSON(secrets) or a dynamic index forces every secret the workflow can see onto the runner, so a single compromised step can read all of them, and log masking is weaker for structured values.

help.text:
Secrets are only sent to a runner when referenced. toJSON(secrets) or a dynamic index forces every secret the workflow can see onto the runner, so a single compromised step can read all of them, and log masking is weaker for structured values.

Remediation: Reference each secret by name, only in the step that needs it.
help.markdown:
Secrets are only sent to a runner when referenced. toJSON(secrets) or a dynamic index forces every secret the workflow can see onto the runner, so a single compromised step can read all of them, and log masking is weaker for structured values.

**Remediation**

rules.name: Hard-coded container registry credentials

shortDescription.text: A job container or service declares a literal password instead of a secret reference.

fullDescription.text: Credentials written into the workflow file are visible to anyone who can read the repository and persist in git history.

help.text:
Credentials written into the workflow file are visible to anyone who can read the repository and persist in git history.

Remediation: Store the password as an Actions secret and reference it as ${{ secrets.NAME }}. Rotate the exposed credential.
help.markdown:
Credentials written into the workflow file are visible to anyone who can read the repository and persist in git history.

**Remediation**

Store the password as an Actions secret and reference it as ${{ secrets.NAME }}. Rotate the exposed credential.

rules.name: Deprecated workflow commands re-enabled

shortDescription.text: ACTIONS_ALLOW_UNSECURE_COMMANDS re-enables ::set-env and ::add-path.

fullDescription.text: With this variable set, any process that prints to stdout — a test, a dependency, a log line containing user text — can set environment variables or PATH for later steps by printing a workflow command.

help.text:
With this variable set, any process that prints to stdout — a test, a dependency, a log line containing user text — can set environment variables or PATH for later steps by printing a workflow command.

Remediation: Remove ACTIONS_ALLOW_UNSECURE_COMMANDS and write to $GITHUB_ENV / $GITHUB_PATH instead.
help.markdown:
With this variable set, any process that prints to stdout — a test, a dependency, a log line containing user text — can set environment variables or PATH for later steps by printing a workflow command.

**Remediation**

rules.name: Authorisation by spoofable actor name

shortDescription.text: An if: trusts github.actor == '<bot>[bot]' in a workflow outsiders can trigger.

fullDescription.text: github.actor is whoever caused the latest event, not who wrote the code. An attacker can open a pull request that a bot later updates (for example by asking Dependabot to rebase), making the bot the actor while the attacker's commits run with the privileges the check was meant to reserve for the bot.

help.text:
github.actor is whoever caused the latest event, not who wrote the code. An attacker can open a pull request that a bot later updates (for example by asking Dependabot to rebase), making the bot the actor while the attacker's commits run with the privileges the check was meant to reserve for the bot.

Remediation: Check the pull request author (github.event.pull_request.user.login) and that the head repository is the base repository, or use the bot's own metadata action.
help.markdown:
github.actor is whoever caused the latest event, not who wrote the code. An attacker can open a pull request that a bot later updates (for example by asking Dependabot to rebase), making the bot the actor while the attacker's commits run with the privileges the check was meant to reserve for the bot.

**Remediation**

Check the pull request author (github.event.pull_request.user.login) and that the head repository is the base repository, or use the bot's own metadata action.

rules.name: Condition always evaluates to true

shortDescription.text: An if: mixes ${{ }} with surrounding text, or is a block scalar, so it is a non-empty string and always true.

fullDescription.text: When an if: value contains text outside a single ${{ }} expression (including a trailing newline from a | block), GitHub evaluates the whole thing as a string, and any non-empty string is truthy. The guard — often an authorisation check — never blocks.

help.text:
When an if: value contains text outside a single ${{ }} expression (including a trailing newline from a | block), GitHub evaluates the whole thing as a string, and any non-empty string is truthy. The guard — often an authorisation check — never blocks.

Remediation: Write the condition as a single expression, either bare (if: a && b) or entirely inside one ${{ }}.
help.markdown:
When an if: value contains text outside a single ${{ }} expression (including a trailing newline from a | block), GitHub evaluates the whole thing as a string, and any non-empty string is truthy. The guard — often an authorisation check — never blocks.

**Remediation**

Write the condition as a single expression, either bare (if: a && b) or entirely inside one ${{ }}.

rules.name: Self-hosted runner reachable from pull requests

shortDescription.text: A job triggered by pull requests runs on a self-hosted runner.

fullDescription.text: Self-hosted runners are not ephemeral by default: code from a pull request can persist on the machine, read credentials from earlier jobs, and reach the internal network the runner sits on. On a public repository any GitHub user can trigger this.

help.text:
Self-hosted runners are not ephemeral by default: code from a pull request can persist on the machine, read credentials from earlier jobs, and reach the internal network the runner sits on. On a public repository any GitHub user can trigger this.

Remediation: Run pull request workflows on GitHub-hosted runners, or on ephemeral (just-in-time) self-hosted runners in an isolated runner group that public repositories cannot use.
help.markdown:
Self-hosted runners are not ephemeral by default: code from a pull request can persist on the machine, read credentials from earlier jobs, and reach the internal network the runner sits on. On a public repository any GitHub user can trigger this.

**Remediation**

Run pull request workflows on GitHub-hosted runners, or on ephemeral (just-in-time) self-hosted runners in an isolated runner group that public repositories cannot use.

**Context used**

- repo
- runner groups

rules.name: Secret printed to the job log

shortDescription.text: A run: step prints a secret, relying on log masking to hide it.

fullDescription.text: Masking only redacts exact matches. Encoded, split or transformed output (base64, JSON, a substring, a multi-line value) is printed in clear to a log readable by everyone with read access.

help.text:
Masking only redacts exact matches. Encoded, split or transformed output (base64, JSON, a substring, a multi-line value) is printed in clear to a log readable by everyone with read access.

Remediation: Never print secrets. Pass them to tools through environment variables or files with restricted permissions.
help.markdown:
Masking only redacts exact matches. Encoded, split or transformed output (base64, JSON, a substring, a multi-line value) is printed in clear to a log readable by everyone with read access.

**Remediation**

Never print secrets. Pass them to tools through environment variables or files with restricted permissions.

rules.name: Comment-triggered workflow without an author check

shortDescription.text: An issue_comment workflow runs privileged steps for any commenter.

fullDescription.text: issue_comment runs with a write token and secrets, and anyone who can comment can trigger it. A ChatOps command (/deploy, /release, /retest) without an author_association or permission check runs for every GitHub user on a public repository.

help.text:
issue_comment runs with a write token and secrets, and anyone who can comment can trigger it. A ChatOps command (/deploy, /release, /retest) without an author_association or permission check runs for every GitHub user on a public repository.

Remediation: Gate the job on github.event.comment.author_association being OWNER, MEMBER or COLLABORATOR, or check the commenter's permission with the API before acting.
help.markdown:
issue_comment runs with a write token and secrets, and anyone who can comment can trigger it. A ChatOps command (/deploy, /release, /retest) without an author_association or permission check runs for every GitHub user on a public repository.

**Remediation**

Gate the job on github.event.comment.author_association being OWNER, MEMBER or COLLABORATOR, or check the commenter's permission with the API before acting.

**Context used**

- repo

rules.name: Obfuscated action reference or expression

shortDescription.text: A uses: path or ${{ }} expression is written in a form that hides what it resolves to.

fullDescription.text: uses: owner/repo/./@ref and github['event']['issue']['title'] resolve to the same thing as their plain forms but evade reviewers, allow-lists and simple scanners. Legitimate workflows rarely need them.

help.text:
uses: owner/repo/./@ref and github['event']['issue']['title'] resolve to the same thing as their plain forms but evade reviewers, allow-lists and simple scanners. Legitimate workflows rarely need them.

Remediation: Write the reference or expression in its plain form.
help.markdown:
uses: owner/repo/./@ref and github['event']['issue']['title'] resolve to the same thing as their plain forms but evade reviewers, allow-lists and simple scanners. Legitimate workflows rarely need them.

**Remediation**

Write the reference or expression in its plain form.

rules.name: Pull request head ref used as a branch or tag name without quoting

shortDescription.text: A shell variable holding the head branch name is passed to git or gh unquoted or without --.

fullDescription.text: Moving an untrusted value into env: fixes script injection, but `git checkout $BRANCH` still lets a branch named --upload-pack=... or -o... inject options. Branch names can start with a dash.

help.text:
Moving an untrusted value into env: fixes script injection, but `git checkout $BRANCH` still lets a branch named --upload-pack=... or -o... inject options. Branch names can start with a dash.

Remediation: Quote the variable and end option parsing: git checkout -- "$BRANCH" (or git switch "refs/heads/$BRANCH").
help.markdown:
Moving an untrusted value into env: fixes script injection, but `git checkout $BRANCH` still lets a branch named --upload-pack=... or -o... inject options. Branch names can start with a dash.

**Remediation**

Quote the variable and end option parsing: git checkout -- "$BRANCH" (or git switch "refs/heads/$BRANCH").

rules.name: Secrets sent to an external host

shortDescription.text: A step sends the secrets context, the environment, or an encoded secret over the network, or sends any secret to a request-capture host or raw IP.

fullDescription.text: Token-theft campaigns add a step that dumps every secret (or the whole environment) and posts it to a server they control, often base64-encoded to slip past log masking, then remove the workflow. Authenticated calls that pass a single secret to an API are not reported; only bulk dumps, encoded secrets, and destinations with no legitimate use are.

help.text:
Token-theft campaigns add a step that dumps every secret (or the whole environment) and posts it to a server they control, often base64-encoded to slip past log masking, then remove the workflow. Authenticated calls that pass a single secret to an API are not reported; only bulk dumps, encoded secrets, and destinations with no legitimate use are.

Remediation: Remove the step and treat every secret available to the workflow as compromised: rotate them, then review who added the change.
help.markdown:
Token-theft campaigns add a step that dumps every secret (or the whole environment) and posts it to a server they control, often base64-encoded to slip past log masking, then remove the workflow. Authenticated calls that pass a single secret to an API are not reported; only bulk dumps, encoded secrets, and destinations with no legitimate use are.

**Remediation**

Remove the step and treat every secret available to the workflow as compromised: rotate them, then review who added the change.

rules.name: Privileged job restores a cache keyed on contributor input

shortDescription.text: In a pull_request_target, workflow_run or comment-triggered job, a cache key or the cached content is derived from the pull request.

fullDescription.text: A key built from the head branch or head SHA lets a contributor choose which entry the privileged job restores; restoring a cache after checking out the pull request saves the contributor's files under a key later trusted runs restore.

help.text:
A key built from the head branch or head SHA lets a contributor choose which entry the privileged job restores; restoring a cache after checking out the pull request saves the contributor's files under a key later trusted runs restore.

Remediation: Key caches only on base-branch content (hashFiles of the base checkout), and do not cache in a job that checked out untrusted code.
help.markdown:
A key built from the head branch or head SHA lets a contributor choose which entry the privileged job restores; restoring a cache after checking out the pull request saves the contributor's files under a key later trusted runs restore.

**Remediation**

Key caches only on base-branch content (hashFiles of the base checkout), and do not cache in a job that checked out untrusted code.

rules.name: Action or reusable workflow not pinned to a commit SHA

shortDescription.text: uses: references a branch or tag, which the action's owner (or anyone who compromises them) can move.

fullDescription.text: Tags and branches are mutable. When an action repository is compromised, the attacker re-points existing tags at malicious code and every workflow referencing them runs it on its next execution — as happened in widely used actions. A full 40-character SHA is the only immutable reference.

help.text:
Tags and branches are mutable. When an action repository is compromised, the attacker re-points existing tags at malicious code and every workflow referencing them runs it on its next execution — as happened in widely used actions. A full 40-character SHA is the only immutable reference.

Remediation: Pin to the full commit SHA and keep the version in a trailing comment (uses: owner/repo@<sha> # v1.2.3); let Dependabot or Renovate update both.
help.markdown:
Tags and branches are mutable. When an action repository is compromised, the attacker re-points existing tags at malicious code and every workflow referencing them runs it on its next execution — as happened in widely used actions. A full 40-character SHA is the only immutable reference.

**Remediation**

Pin to the full commit SHA and keep the version in a trailing comment (uses: owner/repo@<sha> # v1.2.3); let Dependabot or Renovate update both.

- action refs
- actions policy
- repo

rules.name: SHA pin does not match its version comment

shortDescription.text: uses: owner/repo@<sha> # vX.Y.Z, but vX.Y.Z resolves to a different commit.

fullDescription.text: Reviewers and update bots read the version comment, not the SHA. A SHA that does not match its comment either predates an update that only changed the comment, or was swapped deliberately to run a different commit under a trusted-looking version.

help.text:
Reviewers and update bots read the version comment, not the SHA. A SHA that does not match its comment either predates an update that only changed the comment, or was swapped deliberately to run a different commit under a trusted-looking version.

Remediation: Re-pin to the commit the intended version resolves to, and update the comment and SHA together.
help.markdown:
Reviewers and update bots read the version comment, not the SHA. A SHA that does not match its comment either predates an update that only changed the comment, or was swapped deliberately to run a different commit under a trusted-looking version.

**Remediation**

Re-pin to the commit the intended version resolves to, and update the comment and SHA together.

**Context used**

- action refs

rules.name: Pinned commit is not in the action's repository

shortDescription.text: The pinned SHA exists only in a fork of the action repository.

fullDescription.text: GitHub serves commits from any fork through the parent repository's URL. An attacker can push malicious code to a fork and propose a pin to that SHA; it looks like owner/repo@<sha> but the commit was never part of owner/repo.

help.text:
GitHub serves commits from any fork through the parent repository's URL. An attacker can push malicious code to a fork and propose a pin to that SHA; it looks like owner/repo@<sha> but the commit was never part of owner/repo.

Remediation: Replace the SHA with one that is reachable from a branch or tag of the action repository itself.
help.markdown:
GitHub serves commits from any fork through the parent repository's URL. An attacker can push malicious code to a fork and propose a pin to that SHA; it looks like owner/repo@<sha> but the commit was never part of owner/repo.

**Remediation**

Replace the SHA with one that is reachable from a branch or tag of the action repository itself.

**Context used**

- action refs

rules.name: Action repository archived, missing or hijackable

shortDescription.text: The referenced action is archived, deleted, or its owner was renamed or removed.

fullDescription.text: An archived action gets no security fixes. A deleted repository, or an owner that was renamed or removed, lets anyone register the old name and publish code under it (repo-jacking); unpinned references then run it.

help.text:
An archived action gets no security fixes. A deleted repository, or an owner that was renamed or removed, lets anyone register the old name and publish code under it (repo-jacking); unpinned references then run it.

Remediation: Replace the action with a maintained alternative, or vendor it into this repository as a local action.
help.markdown:
An archived action gets no security fixes. A deleted repository, or an owner that was renamed or removed, lets anyone register the old name and publish code under it (repo-jacking); unpinned references then run it.

**Remediation**

fullDescription.text: Actions are dependencies. A vulnerable version — command injection through its inputs, credential leakage, or a compromised release — exposes every workflow that runs it.

help.text:
Actions are dependencies. A vulnerable version — command injection through its inputs, credential leakage, or a compromised release — exposes every workflow that runs it.

Remediation: Upgrade to the fixed version named in the advisory and re-pin to its SHA.
help.markdown:
Actions are dependencies. A vulnerable version — command injection through its inputs, credential leakage, or a compromised release — exposes every workflow that runs it.

**Remediation**

Upgrade to the fixed version named in the advisory and re-pin to its SHA.

**Context used**

- action refs

rules.name: Container image not pinned to a digest

shortDescription.text: docker:// steps, job containers and services reference an image by tag.

fullDescription.text: Image tags are mutable. The image that runs with the job's token and workspace can change without any change to the workflow.

help.text:
Image tags are mutable. The image that runs with the job's token and workspace can change without any change to the workflow.

Remediation: Reference images by digest (image@sha256:...), and let an update bot refresh it.
help.markdown:
Image tags are mutable. The image that runs with the job's token and workspace can change without any change to the workflow.

**Remediation**

Reference images by digest (image@sha256:...), and let an update bot refresh it.

rules.name: Action major version runs on a retired runtime

shortDescription.text: The action version uses a Node.js runtime or backend service GitHub has retired.

fullDescription.text: Retired runtimes receive no security patches and are forced onto newer runtimes by the runner, which can change behaviour; retired artifact and cache backends fail outright.

help.text:
Retired runtimes receive no security patches and are forced onto newer runtimes by the runner, which can change behaviour; retired artifact and cache backends fail outright.

Remediation: Upgrade to the current major version of the action.
help.markdown:
Retired runtimes receive no security patches and are forced onto newer runtimes by the runner, which can change behaviour; retired artifact and cache backends fail outright.

**Remediation**

rules.name: Action not permitted by the allowed-actions policy

shortDescription.text: The workflow references an action that the repository's allowed-actions policy does not list.

fullDescription.text: The run will fail at start-up, or — if the policy is relaxed to make it pass — the allow-list stops meaning anything. Either way the drift should be resolved deliberately.

help.text:
The run will fail at start-up, or — if the policy is relaxed to make it pass — the allow-list stops meaning anything. Either way the drift should be resolved deliberately.

Remediation: Replace the action with an allowed one, or add it (pinned) to the allow-list after review.

**Remediation**

Replace the action with an allowed one, or add it (pinned) to the allow-list after review.

- actions policy

rules.name: Remote script piped into an interpreter

shortDescription.text: A run: step downloads a script and executes it without verifying it.

fullDescription.text: curl | sh runs whatever the server returns at that moment, with the job's token and secrets. A compromised host, CDN or DNS response becomes code execution in CI.

help.text:
curl | sh runs whatever the server returns at that moment, with the job's token and secrets. A compromised host, CDN or DNS response becomes code execution in CI.

Remediation: Download to a file, verify a pinned checksum or signature, then execute it — or use a pinned action or package instead.
help.markdown:
curl | sh runs whatever the server returns at that moment, with the job's token and secrets. A compromised host, CDN or DNS response becomes code execution in CI.

**Remediation**

Download to a file, verify a pinned checksum or signature, then execute it — or use a pinned action or package instead.

rules.name: Default branch is not protected

shortDescription.text: Neither branch protection nor a ruleset applies to the default branch.

fullDescription.text: Anyone with write access — including a compromised token, a leaked deploy key, or a workflow with contents: write — can push directly to the default branch, rewrite its history or delete it, and the change ships without review.

help.text:
Anyone with write access — including a compromised token, a leaked deploy key, or a workflow with contents: write — can push directly to the default branch, rewrite its history or delete it, and the change ships without review.

Remediation: Add a ruleset targeting the default branch that requires pull requests with at least one approval, blocks force pushes and deletions, and requires status checks.

Anyone with write access — including a compromised token, a leaked deploy key, or a workflow with contents: write — can push directly to the default branch, rewrite its history or delete it, and the change ships without review.
